newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: INTERVIEW-Compaq eyes lower-end PC market in Asia.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Compaq eyes lower-end PC market in Asia.

text.p: U.S.-based Compaq Computer Corp is aiming to boost its Asian market share in lower-priced personal computers, a senior company official said on Thursday.

"If you look at the price bands out there, between US$600-1,600 range there is a big market. In some countries those markets can be as big as 60-70 percent (of the whole computer market), like in India and China," Paul Chan said.

"That segment of the market is still quite closed to us. We want to be very competitive to be able to offer PCs to a broader group of people," Chan, Compaq's vice president and managing director, Asia Pacific, told Reuters in an interview.
He said technology companies from countries like Taiwan and South Korea now dominated the lower-priced market.
Chan said Compaq's recent move towards build-to-order and build-to-configure manufacturing strategy would help towards this goal by lowering cost and bringing more flexibility.
He said manufacturing processes in the Asia Pacific region, where Compaq has three plants, would be change towards build-to-order and build-to-configure but could not specify when this would happen.
But the first products from this process are expected to roll out in summer.
"It's a clear direction we need to move more towards on-demand manufacturing that offers a lot more flexibility," he said.
Chan said in 1996 Compaq had a seven percent market share in the Asia Pacific region for its PCs and servers. Servers alone garnered a share of about 25 percent.
Revenues from the region contributed about six percent to global sales of US$18.1 billion in 1996, he said.
"By year 2000, we would like to step up to 10-15 percent," he said.

Compaq would like to see double digit market shares in its Asian markets, especially countries like China, India, Indonesia and Philippines where the bulk of demand was for the US$600-S$1,600 range of products, Chan said.
He added that the company had already achieved double-digit shares in Hong Kong, Singapore and New Zealand.
Chan told a news conference later that Compaq would increase its sales force in the region for more direct dealings with corporate customers.
But dealers, distributors and channel partners continue to be important in the installation and implementation of systems.

On Thursday, Compaq launched a US$3.0 million centre in Singapore that showcases business applications put together with its partners. Company officials added that more such centres would be set up in the region.
